title: Long live cash: why Japan is in no hurry to go cashless

words.ctx: In much of the rich world, tapping a phone has replaced fumbling for coins.

ex.en: He [[fumbled for]] his keys in the dark.
ex.zh: 他在黑暗里摸索着找钥匙。

ex.en: She stood at the gate, [[fumbling for]] her ticket.
ex.zh: 她站在检票口，在包里摸索着找车票。

cloze.before: In much of the rich world, tapping a phone has replaced
cloze.after: for coins.
cloze.szh: 在富裕世界的大部分地方，轻点手机已经取代了摸索着找硬币。

words.note: 反义词 irrational 出现在全文倒数第四句。
words.ctx: In Japan the old habit survives for reasons that are more rational than they look.

ex.en: It was a [[rational]] decision, not an emotional one.
ex.zh: 那是个理性的决定，不是感情用事。

ex.en: Few people stay fully [[rational]] when they are afraid.
ex.zh: 很少有人在害怕的时候还能完全保持理性。

cloze.before: In Japan the old habit survives for reasons that are more
cloze.after: than they look.
cloze.szh: 在日本，这个老习惯留存下来，理由比看上去的更理性。

words.ctx: Some customers wave a phone at the reader; a surprising number still count out coins with the unhurried air of people who have nowhere to be.

ex.en: She [[counted out]] ten coins onto the counter.
ex.zh: 她把十枚硬币一枚一枚数到柜台上。

ex.en: The cashier [[counted out]] the change slowly.
ex.zh: 收银员慢慢地数出找零。

ex.en: She walked at an [[unhurried]] pace along the river.
ex.zh: 她沿着河边不紧不慢地走。

ex.en: His [[unhurried]] manner calmed the whole room.
ex.zh: 他从容的态度让整个房间都平静下来。

words.ctx: Some customers wave a phone at the reader; a surprising number still count out coins with the unhurried air of people who have nowhere to be.

ex.en: He spoke with an [[air of]] quiet authority.
ex.zh: 他说话时带着一种沉稳的权威感。

ex.en: The old house had an [[air of]] neglect.
ex.zh: 那座老房子有一种无人照管的气息。

words.ctx: To a visitor from Shenzhen or Stockholm, where cash has become a rarity, the scene looks like a time capsule.

ex.en: Handwritten letters have become [[a rarity]].
ex.zh: 手写信已经成了稀罕物。

ex.en: Honest feedback is [[a rarity]] in some offices.
ex.zh: 在有些办公室里，坦率的反馈很难得。

cloze.before: To a visitor from Shenzhen or Stockholm, where cash has become a
cloze.after: , the scene looks like a time capsule.
cloze.szh: 对来自深圳或斯德哥尔摩的游客来说，那些地方现金已经很少见，眼前的场景就像一个时间胶囊。

words.zh: 时间胶囊；保留旧时代原貌的地方
words.ctx: To a visitor from Shenzhen or Stockholm, where cash has become a rarity, the scene looks like a time capsule.

ex.en: The restored cafe feels like a [[time capsule]] from the 1960s.
ex.zh: 这家修复过的咖啡馆像一个来自六十年代的时间胶囊。

ex.en: The pupils buried a [[time capsule]] under the school garden.
ex.zh: 学生们在学校花园下埋了一个时间胶囊。

cloze.before: To a visitor from Shenzhen or Stockholm, where cash has become a rarity, the scene looks like a time
cloze.szh: 对来自深圳或斯德哥尔摩的游客来说，那些地方现金已经很少见，眼前的场景就像一个时间胶囊。

words.note: 常用结构 coax sb into doing sth；也可以 coax sb to do sth。
words.ctx: Japan's officials see it differently, and have spent years trying to coax shoppers into going cashless.

ex.en: She [[coaxed]] the shy cat out from under the sofa.
ex.zh: 她把害羞的猫从沙发底下哄了出来。

ex.en: He tried to [[coax]] his grandmother into using a smartphone.
ex.zh: 他想哄着奶奶用上智能手机。

cloze.before: Japan's officials see it differently, and have spent years trying to
cloze.after: shoppers into going cashless.
cloze.szh: 日本的官员看法不同，多年来一直想哄着顾客改用无现金支付。

words.ctx: The first reason is that cash works remarkably well here.

ex.en: The patient recovered [[remarkably]] quickly.
ex.zh: 病人恢复得出奇地快。

ex.en: The two reports are [[remarkably]] similar.
ex.zh: 这两份报告惊人地相似。

cloze.before: The first reason is that cash works
cloze.after: well here.
cloze.szh: 第一个原因是，现金在这里用起来出奇地好。

words.note: notes 是英式的“纸币”，美式常说 a wad of bills。
words.ctx: Crime is low, so carrying a thick wad of notes feels safe, and cash machines are everywhere, including in almost every convenience store.

ex.en: He pulled a [[wad of notes]] from his coat pocket.
ex.zh: 他从外套口袋里掏出一沓钞票。

ex.en: The thief fled with a thick [[wad of notes]].
ex.zh: 小偷带着厚厚一沓钞票逃走了。

cloze.before: Crime is low, so carrying a thick
cloze.after: of notes feels safe, and cash machines are everywhere, including in almost every convenience store.
cloze.szh: 犯罪率低，所以带着厚厚一沓钞票也觉得安全；取款机到处都是，几乎每家便利店里都有。

words.ctx: Cash also keeps working when the power fails, which counts for something in a country that lives with earthquakes.

ex.en: Experience still [[counts for something]] in this business.
ex.zh: 在这一行里，经验仍然是有分量的。

ex.en: Her opinion [[counts for something]] around here.
ex.zh: 她的意见在这里是说得上话的。

cloze.before: Cash also keeps working when the power fails, which
cloze.after: for something in a country that lives with earthquakes.
cloze.szh: 停电的时候，现金照样能用，在一个与地震共存的国家，这一点是有分量的。

words.note: make up 还有“化妆”“编造”“和好”等意思，这里是“占……”。
words.ctx: Older customers, who make up a growing share of the population, tend to trust what they can hold in their hands.

ex.en: Students [[make up]] nearly half of the audience.
ex.zh: 学生占了观众的近一半。

ex.en: Women [[make up]] a growing share of the workforce.
ex.zh: 女性在劳动力中的占比越来越大。

cloze.before: Older customers, who
cloze.after: up a growing share of the population, tend to trust what they can hold in their hands.
cloze.szh: 年长的顾客在人口中占比越来越大，他们往往更信任手里能握住的东西。

words.ctx: Older customers, who make up a growing share of the population, tend to trust what they can hold in their hands.

ex.en: Prices [[tend to]] rise before the holidays.
ex.zh: 价格往往在假期前上涨。

ex.en: He [[tends to]] speak quickly when he is nervous.
ex.zh: 他一紧张就容易说得很快。

cloze.before: Older customers, who make up a growing share of the population,
cloze.after: to trust what they can hold in their hands.
cloze.szh: 年长的顾客在人口中占比越来越大，他们往往更信任手里能握住的东西。

words.ctx: The second reason is that the bill for convenience lands on someone else.

ex.en: The blame for the delay [[landed on]] the project manager.
ex.zh: 延误的责任落到了项目经理头上。

ex.en: If the order is wrong, the cost [[lands on]] the supplier.
ex.zh: 订单要是出错，成本就落在供应商头上。

cloze.before: The second reason is that the bill for convenience
cloze.after: on someone else.
cloze.szh: 第二个原因是，方便的账单落到了别人头上。

words.ctx: Shoppers pay nothing extra to use cash, whereas shops hand over a slice of every card sale to the firms that run the payment networks.

ex.en: Please [[hand over]] your passport at the desk.
ex.zh: 请在前台交出您的护照。

ex.en: The company had to [[hand over]] all its records to the regulator.
ex.zh: 公司不得不把全部记录交给监管机构。

cloze.before: Shoppers pay nothing extra to use cash, whereas shops
cloze.after: over a slice of every card sale to the firms that run the payment networks.
cloze.szh: 顾客用现金不用多付一分钱，而商家每做成一笔刷卡生意，都要把一部分交给运营支付网络的公司。

words.zh: 一份、一部分（常指分走的那一份）
words.ctx: Shoppers pay nothing extra to use cash, whereas shops hand over a slice of every card sale to the firms that run the payment networks.

ex.en: The agency takes [[a slice of]] every sale.
ex.zh: 中介从每一笔销售里抽走一份。

ex.en: Tourism brings the town [[a slice of]] new income.
ex.zh: 旅游给这个小镇带来了一部分新收入。

cloze.before: Shoppers pay nothing extra to use cash, whereas shops hand over a
cloze.after: of every card sale to the firms that run the payment networks.
cloze.szh: 顾客用现金不用多付一分钱，而商家每做成一笔刷卡生意，都要把一部分交给运营支付网络的公司。

words.note: 对应说法：fat margins（利润丰厚）。
words.ctx: For a small bakery working on thin margins, that slice can be the difference between a profit and a loss.

ex.en: Supermarkets operate on [[thin margins]].
ex.zh: 超市是靠微薄的利润率运转的。

ex.en: Small farms with [[thin margins]] cannot survive a bad harvest.
ex.zh: 利润微薄的小农场扛不住一次歉收。

cloze.before: For a small bakery working on
cloze.after: margins, that slice can be the difference between a profit and a loss.
cloze.szh: 对一家利润微薄的小面包店来说，这一份抽成可能就是盈利与亏损的差别。

words.ctx: Many owners therefore accept cards grudgingly, and a few quietly discourage them.

ex.en: He [[grudgingly]] admitted that she was right.
ex.zh: 他勉强承认她是对的。

ex.en: The council [[grudgingly]] approved the plan.
ex.zh: 市议会不情不愿地批准了这个计划。

cloze.before: Many owners therefore accept cards
cloze.after: , and a few quietly discourage them.
cloze.szh: 因此，许多店主勉强接受刷卡，还有少数人悄悄地劝阻顾客别刷卡。

words.ctx: Many owners therefore accept cards grudgingly, and a few quietly discourage them.

ex.en: High fees [[discourage]] young people from saving.
ex.zh: 高额费用让年轻人不愿存钱。

ex.en: Her parents [[discouraged]] her from leaving school.
ex.zh: 她的父母劝她不要退学。

cloze.before: Many owners therefore accept cards grudgingly, and a few quietly
cloze.after: them.
cloze.szh: 因此，许多店主勉强接受刷卡，还有少数人悄悄地劝阻顾客别刷卡。

words.note: 行为经济学里的 nudge（助推）指不强制、只改变选择环境的引导方式。
words.ctx: Officials have long tried to nudge people along.

ex.en: The new rules aim to [[nudge]] drivers towards electric cars.
ex.zh: 新规定的目的是引导司机转向电动车。

ex.en: A friendly reminder can [[nudge]] people to pay on time.
ex.zh: 一条友好的提醒就能促使人们按时付款。

cloze.before: Officials have long tried to
cloze.after: people along.
cloze.szh: 官员们早就想把人们往前推一推。

words.note: dangle sth in front of sb：把好处摆在某人面前来引诱。
words.ctx: A few years ago the government dangled rebates in front of anyone who paid by card or phone, and the share of cashless payments crept upward.

ex.en: The airline [[dangled]] free upgrades to win over business travellers.
ex.zh: 航空公司拿免费升舱来争取商务旅客。

ex.en: The manager [[dangled]] the prospect of a promotion in front of her staff.
ex.zh: 经理在员工面前吊着晋升的前景。

cloze.before: A few years ago the government

words.ctx: A few years ago the government dangled rebates in front of anyone who paid by card or phone, and the share of cashless payments crept upward.

ex.en: Buyers of electric cars receive a [[rebate]] from the state.
ex.zh: 电动车的买家能从政府那里拿到一笔返还款。

ex.en: The shop offers [[rebates]] on bulk orders.
ex.zh: 这家店对大宗订单提供返利。

words.ctx: A few years ago the government dangled rebates in front of anyone who paid by card or phone, and the share of cashless payments crept upward.

ex.en: Inflation has been [[creeping upward]] all year.
ex.zh: 通胀一整年都在缓慢上升。

ex.en: Unemployment [[crept upward]] for three months in a row.
ex.zh: 失业率连续三个月缓慢上升。

cloze.before: A few years ago the government dangled rebates in front of anyone who paid by card or phone, and the share of cashless payments

words.ctx: But incentives of that kind tend to fade once the money runs out.

ex.en: The excitement began to [[fade]] after the first week.
ex.zh: 头一个星期过后，兴奋劲儿开始消退。

ex.en: The sound of the music slowly [[faded]] away.
ex.zh: 音乐声慢慢地消失了。

cloze.before: But incentives of that kind tend to
cloze.after: once the money runs out.
cloze.szh: 但这类激励措施往往在钱花完之后就慢慢失效了。

words.note: run out of sth 才是“用完了某物”，run out 的主语是被用完的东西。
words.ctx: But incentives of that kind tend to fade once the money runs out.

ex.en: We must finish before the funding [[runs out]].
ex.zh: 我们必须在资金用完之前完成。

ex.en: The patience of the voters finally [[ran out]].
ex.zh: 选民们的耐心终于耗尽了。

cloze.before: But incentives of that kind tend to fade once the money
cloze.after: out.

words.ctx: What may finally tip the balance is not persuasion but arithmetic.

ex.en: One late goal [[tipped the balance]] in their favour.
ex.zh: 一个绝杀球让天平倒向了他们这边。

ex.en: A small tax cut could [[tip the balance]] for undecided voters.
ex.zh: 小小的减税就可能让犹豫不决的选民做出决定。

cloze.before: What may finally
cloze.after: the balance is not persuasion but arithmetic.
cloze.szh: 最终可能打破平衡的，不是劝说，而是算账。

words.ctx: What may finally tip the balance is not persuasion but arithmetic.

ex.en: The [[arithmetic]] of the deal simply does not work.
ex.zh: 这笔交易的账怎么算都算不过来。

ex.en: Do the [[arithmetic]] before you sign the lease.
ex.zh: 签租约之前先把账算清楚。

cloze.before: What may finally tip the balance is not persuasion but
cloze.szh: 最终可能打破平衡的，不是劝说，而是算账。

words.ctx: Japan's workforce is shrinking, and every hour a shopkeeper spends counting the till costs more each year.

ex.en: The town's population has [[shrunk]] by a third.
ex.zh: 这个镇的人口减少了三分之一。

ex.en: Profits [[shrank]] as costs rose.
ex.zh: 成本上升，利润随之缩水。

cloze.before: Japan's workforce is
cloze.after: , and every hour a shopkeeper spends counting the till costs more each year.
cloze.szh: 日本的劳动力在减少，店主每花一个小时清点收银抽屉，成本都一年比一年高。

words.note: till 还可以作介词，意思和 until 一样；作名词时是英式的“收银机”。
words.ctx: Japan's workforce is shrinking, and every hour a shopkeeper spends counting the till costs more each year.

ex.en: The cashier counted the [[till]] at closing time.
ex.zh: 收银员在打烊时清点了收银抽屉。

ex.en: Someone had taken money from the [[till]].
ex.zh: 有人从收银抽屉里拿走了钱。

cloze.before: Japan's workforce is shrinking, and every hour a shopkeeper spends counting the

cloze.szh: 日本的劳动力在减少，店主每花一个小时清点收银抽屉，成本都一年比一年高。

words.note: ferry sth about / around：把东西来回运送。
words.ctx: Handling cash is a hidden expense: notes must be counted, banked and ferried about in armoured vans, and someone has to keep all those machines topped up.

ex.en: Minibuses [[ferry]] guests between the hotel and the beach.
ex.zh: 小巴在酒店和海滩之间接送客人。

ex.en: Volunteers [[ferried]] supplies to the village by boat.
ex.zh: 志愿者们用船把物资运到村子里。

cloze.before: Handling cash is a hidden expense: notes must be counted, banked and

cloze.szh: 处理现金是一笔隐形开支：纸币要清点、存入银行、用运钞车运来运去，还得有人把那些取款机一直补满。

words.ctx: Handling cash is a hidden expense: notes must be counted, banked and ferried about in armoured vans, and someone has to keep all those machines topped up.

ex.en: I need to [[top up]] my travel card.
ex.zh: 我得给交通卡充值。

ex.en: The nurse [[topped up]] the water jug.

words.ctx: None of this makes Japan's attachment to cash irrational.

ex.en: Her [[attachment to]] the old village never faded.
ex.zh: 她对老村子的依恋从未淡去。

ex.en: Voters' [[attachment to]] their local hospital is strong.
ex.zh: 选民们对本地医院的感情很深。

cloze.before: None of this makes Japan's
cloze.after: to cash irrational.
cloze.szh: 这一切都不会让日本人对现金的依恋变得不理性。

words.ctx: People stick with what works, and the cost of switching is easy to overlook for those who stand to gain from it.

ex.en: I'll [[stick with]] the plan until it clearly fails.
ex.zh: 在计划明显行不通之前，我会坚持用它。

ex.en: Many fans [[stuck with]] the team through the bad years.
ex.zh: 许多球迷在那些低谷的年头也一直支持这支球队。

cloze.before: People

cloze.szh: 人们会坚持用管用的东西，而改用新办法的成本，对那些能从中获益的人来说，很容易被忽略。

words.note: overlook 还有“俯瞰”的意思：a hotel overlooking the sea。
words.ctx: People stick with what works, and the cost of switching is easy to overlook for those who stand to gain from it.

words.ctx: People stick with what works, and the cost of switching is easy to overlook for those who stand to gain from it.

words.note: give way (to sth)：（对……）让步；英式里也指“给别的车辆让路”。
words.ctx: Habits rarely give way because someone has made a persuasive case; they do so when the old way becomes more expensive for those who set the price.

ex.en: The old rules finally [[gave way]] to a simpler system.
ex.zh: 旧规定终于让位给了一套更简单的制度。

ex.en: Her anger [[gave way]] to sadness.
ex.zh: 她的愤怒渐渐变成了悲伤。

cloze.szh: 习惯很少是因为有人提出了有说服力的论证才让步；它们让步，是在旧方式对那些定价的人变得更贵的时候。

words.note: 常见变化：make a strong case for sth（为……提出有力的论证）。
words.ctx: Habits rarely give way because someone has made a persuasive case; they do so when the old way becomes more expensive for those who set the price.

ex.en: Lawyers [[make a case]] on behalf of their clients.
ex.zh: 律师替当事人陈述理由。

ex.en: The author [[makes a case]] for slower, deeper reading.
ex.zh: 作者为更慢、更深入的阅读提出了论证。

words.note: 也可以写成 stand-off；《经济学人》多写 standoff。
words.ctx: Until then, the bakery queue will remain a quiet standoff between two ways of paying.

ex.en: The strike ended a six-week [[standoff]] between the union and the firm.
ex.zh: 罢工结束了工会与公司之间长达六周的僵持。

ex.en: A tense [[standoff]] followed at the border.
ex.zh: 边境上随后出现了一场紧张的对峙。
